sessions.title: Would You Trust an AI Agent With This?
sessions.description:
Experience Agentic AI in action within IBM Concert for Z and see how AI can accelerate problem determination by analyzing system signals, identifying likely causes, gathering evidence, and recommending next steps. After the live demonstration, participate in a quick interactive voting exercise where you'll decide whether specific operational tasks should be automated by AI, assisted by AI, or remain under human control.
This engaging session explores the evolving relationship between human expertise and AI-driven operations, highlighting how Agentic AI can help address knowledge gaps,reduce reliance on specialized experts, and improve decision-making across complex environments. Attendees will gain insight into the practical applications of autonomous operations while helping shape the future direction of Concert for Z's Agentic AI capabilities.

sessions.title: Software Management-as-Code - IBM Z Install
sessions.description:
Experience a hands-on demonstration of IBM Z Install and see how software management can be transformed through a GitOps-driven, software management-as-code approach. Attendees will explore a prototype that uses standard repositories to configure, deploy, and track z/OS software across partitions, providing a centralized inventory of what is installed, where it is running, and how it was deployed.

The session showcases a self-service, AI-assisted experience that brings together software installation, governance, and auditability using industry-standard workflows. Learn how IBM is extending Infrastructure-as-Code, Configuration-as-Code, and Policy-as-Code principles to z/OS software management, helping organizations improve visibility, streamline operations, and accelerate time to value while maintaining business controls and compliance.

sessions.description:
Explore how IBM Project Polaris is extending As-Code practices across z/OS, moving beyond isolated configuration tasks to support Networking, Storage Management, Workload Manager (WLM), and other core system domains. sessions.title: From Client Configuration Data to Simplification Signals
sessions.description:
The IBM Z Configuration Collection Program demonstrates how real-world client configuration data can be used to identify opportunities for simplification across the platform. This exhibit showcases how IBM has analyzed customer configuration data and identified a subset of configuration settings as candidates for simplification, helping teams better understand where complexity exists and where focused improvements may provide the greatest value.

Attendees will see how these insights are already being used to inform IBM Z simplification efforts and explore how configuration intelligence could influence future capabilities such as Project Polaris and the z/OS configuration registry. Visitors will also have the opportunity to discuss their own configuration challenges and help shape future priorities for reducing friction, improving usability, and simplifying system management.
